questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

The following diagram shows a circle with centre O and radius 4 cm.

[Diagram not to scale: P, Q and R lie on the circumference. Arc PQR bounds the shaded major sector and angle PÔR = θ at O.]

The points P, Q and R lie on the circumference of the circle and PÔR = θ, where θ is measured in radians. The length of arc PQR is 10 cm.

(a) Find the perimeter of the shaded sector. [2]

(b) Find θ. [2]

(c) Find the area of the shaded sector. [2]
questions.summary: Calculate a sector's perimeter, angle and area from its arc length.
questions.solution: (a) Perimeter=10+2(4)=18 cm. (b) Using s=rθ, θ=10/4=5/2 radians. (c) Area=(1/2)r²θ=(1/2)(16)(5/2)=20 cm².

questions.accessible_text:
2. [Maximum mark: 6]

Consider an arithmetic sequence with u₁ = 0.6 and u₄ = 0.15.

(a) Find the common difference, d. [2]

The following table shows the probability distribution of a discrete random variable X such that P(X = n) = uₙ/k, where n ∈ ℤ⁺, 1 ≤ n ≤ 4 and k ∈ ℝ⁺.

n          | 1     | 2     | 3    | 4
P(X = n)   | 0.6/k | u₂/k  | u₃/k | 0.15/k

(b) Find the value of k. [4]
questions.summary: Use an arithmetic sequence to normalize a probability distribution.
questions.solution: (a) 0.15=0.6+3d, so d=−0.15. Thus the four terms are 0.6,0.45,0.30,0.15. (b) Their probabilities sum to 1, so (1.5)/k=1 and k=1.5.

questions.accessible_text:
3. [Maximum mark: 5]

A function f is defined by f(x) = 1 − 1/(x − 2), where x ∈ ℝ, x ≠ 2.

(a) The graph of y = f(x) has a vertical asymptote and a horizontal asymptote. Write down the equation of
    (i) the vertical asymptote;
    (ii) the horizontal asymptote. [2]

(b) Find the coordinates of the point where the graph of y = f(x) intersects
    (i) the y-axis;
    (ii) the x-axis. [2]

(c) On the provided axes, sketch the graph of y = f(x), showing all the features found in parts (a) and (b). [1]
questions.summary: Identify asymptotes and intercepts and sketch a translated reciprocal graph.
questions.solution: (a)(i) x=2. (ii) y=1. (b)(i) f(0)=3/2, so (0,3/2). (ii) 1−1/(x−2)=0 gives x=3, so (3,0). (c) Draw the two reciprocal branches approaching x=2 and y=1 and passing through the stated intercepts.

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 5]

Events A and B are such that P(A) = 0.4, P(A | B) = 0.25 and P(A ∪ B) = 0.55.

Find P(B).
questions.summary: Combine conditional probability with the addition rule.
questions.solution: Let p=P(B). Then P(A∩B)=P(A|B)P(B)=0.25p. The addition rule gives 0.55=0.4+p−0.25p, so 0.75p=0.15 and P(B)=0.2.

questions.accessible_text:
5. [Maximum mark: 6]

The following diagram shows part of the graph of y = 2x/(x² + 2) for x ≥ 0.

[Diagram: the curve and x-axis bound a shaded region R from x=0 to the vertical line x=c.]

The shaded region R is bounded by the curve, the x-axis and the line x = c. The area of R is ln 3.

Find the value of c.
questions.summary: Use a definite integral and logarithm laws to determine a boundary.
questions.solution: Area = ∫₀ᶜ 2x/(x²+2) dx = [ln(x²+2)]₀ᶜ = ln((c²+2)/2). Equating to ln3 gives (c²+2)/2=3, so c²=4. Since c≥0, c=2.

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 7]

The functions f and g are defined for x ∈ ℝ by

f(x) = ax + b, where a, b ∈ ℤ,
g(x) = x² + x + 3.

Find the two possible functions f such that (g ∘ f)(x) = 4x² − 14x + 15.
questions.summary: Determine linear functions from a prescribed quadratic composition.
questions.solution: g(f(x))=(ax+b)²+(ax+b)+3=a²x²+a(2b+1)x+(b²+b+3). Hence a²=4 and a(2b+1)=−14. If a=2, b=−4; if a=−2, b=3. Both give the required constant term, so f(x)=2x−4 or f(x)=−2x+3.

questions.accessible_text:
7. [Maximum mark: 17]

The following diagram shows part of the graph of a quadratic function f. The vertex of the parabola is (−2, −5) and the y-intercept is at point P.

[Diagram: an upward-opening parabola with vertex (−2,−5), crossing the y-axis at P.]

(a) Write down the equation of the axis of symmetry. [1]

The function can be written in the form f(x) = (1/4)(x − h)² + k, where h, k ∈ ℤ.

(b) Write down the values of h and k. [2]

(c) Find the y-coordinate of P. [2]

In the following diagram, the line L is normal to the graph of f at point P.

[Diagram: the normal L passes through P and intersects the parabola again at Q.]

(d) Find the equation of the line L, in the form y = ax + b. [4]

(e) Calculate the distance between P and Q. [8]
questions.summary: Use vertex form and differentiation to find a normal and a second intersection.
questions.solution: (a) x=−2. (b) h=−2, k=−5, so f(x)=(1/4)(x+2)²−5. (c) f(0)=−4, so P=(0,−4). (d) f′(x)=(x+2)/2, hence the tangent gradient at P is 1 and the normal gradient is −1. Thus L: y=−x−4. (e) Solving (1/4)(x+2)²−5=−x−4 gives x(x+8)=0. The second point is Q=(−8,4). Therefore PQ=√[8²+8²]=8√2.

8. [Maximum mark: 14]

Consider an acute angle θ such that cos θ = 2/3.

(a) Find the value of
    (i) sin θ;
    (ii) sin 2θ. [4]

The following diagram shows triangle ABC, with B̂ = θ, Â = 2θ, BC = a and AC = b.

[Diagram: triangle ABC with side BC labelled a, side AC labelled b, angle B=θ and angle A=2θ.]

(b) Show that b/a = 3/4. [2]

[BA] is extended to form an isosceles triangle DAC, with D̂ = θ, as shown in the following diagram.

[Diagram: B, A and D are collinear; triangle DAC is isosceles, with angles at C and D each θ.]

(c) Find the value of sin CÂD. [3]

(d) Find the area of triangle DAC, in terms of a. [5]
questions.summary: Apply trigonometric identities, the sine rule and an area formula.
questions.solution: (a)(i) sinθ=√(1−4/9)=√5/3. (ii) sin2θ=2sinθcosθ=4√5/9. (b) By the sine rule, b/a=sinθ/sin2θ=(√5/3)/(4√5/9)=3/4. (c) CÂD is supplementary to 2θ, so sin(CÂD)=sin2θ=4√5/9. (d) In isosceles DAC, AD=AC=b=3a/4. Area=(1/2)b²sin(CÂD)=(1/2)(9a²/16)(4√5/9)=√5a²/8.

questions.accessible_text:
9. [Maximum mark: 14]

A circle with equation x² + y² = 9 has centre (0, 0) and radius 3. A triangle, PQR, is inscribed in the circle with its vertices at P(−3, 0), Q(x, y) and R(x, −y), where Q and R are variable points in the first and fourth quadrants respectively.

[Diagram: P is the leftmost point of the circle; Q and R are vertically aligned on the right, forming triangle PQR.]

(a) For point Q, show that y = √(9 − x²). [1]

(b) Hence, find an expression for A, the area of triangle PQR, in terms of x. [3]

(c) Show that dA/dx = (9 − 3x − 2x²)/√(9 − x²). [4]

(d) Hence or otherwise, find the y-coordinate of R such that A is a maximum. [6]
questions.summary: Optimize the area of a triangle inscribed in a circle.
questions.solution: (a) Since Q lies on x²+y²=9 and y>0, y=√(9−x²). (b) Base QR=2y and perpendicular height from P is x+3, so A=(1/2)(2√(9−x²))(x+3)=(x+3)√(9−x²). (c) Product and chain rules give A′=√(9−x²)−x(x+3)/√(9−x²)=(9−3x−2x²)/√(9−x²). (d) Set the numerator to zero: 2x²+3x−9=(2x−3)(x+3)=0. In the first quadrant x=3/2. Point R has y-coordinate −√(9−9/4)=−3√3/2.
